pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
What we collect

When you ask for a bay we keep your name, email address, preferred car park, vehicle make and model and the month you would like to start. We keep nothing else about you before a contract begins.

How we use it

We keep the details you send in a bay request only to answer that request and to run your contract. We do not sell them or share them for advertising.

How long we keep it

Requests that do not lead to a contract are deleted within six months. Contract records are kept for as long as the law asks of us, and then removed.

Your choices

You can ask to see, correct or delete what we hold by writing to the office at 18 Canal Street, Northgate. We reply within two working days.

pages.title: Terms
pages.content:
The agreement

Monthly bays are let under a written agreement that starts on the 1st or 15th of the month and ends with thirty days' notice. The agreement you sign is the one that applies.

Using your bay

The bay is for the vehicle registered on your agreement. It may not be sublet or passed to anyone else, and loose goods may not be stored on it.

Fees and deposit

Fees are billed monthly in advance. The key fob deposit of thirty euros is returned when the undamaged fob is handed back to the office.

Insurance

Your vehicle and its contents remain your responsibility. Please keep valid road insurance for the whole term of the agreement.

posts.title: The nurse on nights
posts.excerpt: A night-shift nurse explains how an allocated covered bay at Northgate Station brought calm routine to demanding hospital hours.
posts.content:
At dusk in central Northgate, traffic moves slowly around Station Approach as rail commuters head home. For local hospital staff arriving for an overnight nursing shift, finding a kerbside parking space used to mean driving through surrounding residential streets in the cold. Metered spaces carried strict time restrictions, pay-and-display machines broke down, and leaving a vehicle on an unlit side road until morning brought steady worry during demanding clinical work.

When an overnight nurse applied for a monthly bay through Teisha Parking, she was looking for steady routine rather than good fortune. Founded in 2009, Teisha Parking manages 412 monthly bays across six town car parks, with Northgate Station providing 96 of those spaces. Instead of dealing with an automated parking portal or impersonal ticket machines, she completed our single application form and received a personal reply from Priya Nair within 2 working days. Soon after, she met founder Mara Lindqvist on site for a 20 minutes walk to inspect the car park on foot before signing any agreement.

During that walking visit, they inspected an available covered bay at Northgate Station. Mara showed how the electronic barrier key fob worked and walked the illuminated pedestrian path leading directly toward Station Approach and local transport links. They checked the overhead lamps, confirmed that car doors opened comfortably without touching pillars, and reviewed the contract details: a covered bay at €135 monthly, a one-off deposit of €30 for the barrier key fob, and a rolling agreement requiring 30 days notice.

Having an allocated space open 24 hours daily changed the nurse's working routine immediately. Arriving at the car park before handover, the barrier arm lifts smoothly to her electronic key fob. The covered bays remain sheltered from rain and autumn leaves, and her assigned bay is always vacant and waiting. There is no searching for a space, no rush to beat evening railway commuters, and no meter to check. On cold winter nights when frost forms across Northgate, the vehicle stays protected under the roof, saving precious minutes after work.

Returning to the car after the night shift brings the same quiet reliability. Northgate Station remains illuminated throughout the dark hours, with clean tarmac and clear sightlines maintained by Tomás Reyes and the operations team. The nurse knows that if any maintenance need arises, our staff are always attentive. For drivers working outside standard daytime business hours, having an assigned bay that belongs strictly to them removes unnecessary friction from the daily commute.

A rolling monthly contract starting on either the 1st or the 15th gives shift workers flexibility without long annual commitments. With contracts prepared by Aiko Brandt and accounts looked after by Lena Fischer, every administrative detail remains straightforward and predictable. Knowing that your journey begins and ends in a calm, orderly car park provides real peace of mind. It is a practical business arrangement built on quiet order, clear rules, and personal respect across our Northgate car parks.

posts.title: Two vans, one bakery
posts.excerpt: A town bakery needs wide bays and early access, and two delivery vans load at Riverside Depot every morning.
posts.content:
A small bakery loads before dawn and needs room to turn. Riverside Depot gives its two vans wide bays and an automatic gate that works at any hour.

The bakery took both bays on one agreement, starting on the 1st.

posts.title: Charging by the library
posts.excerpt: Working across several town offices, one driver keeps an assigned charging bay at Library Square for the day and overnight.
posts.content:
Moving between town offices makes charging part of the working day. An assigned EV bay at Library Square means the car is ready when she is.

The bay costs €165 a month, with the same thirty days' notice as every other.
